highlights: ## The $1.2 million experiment demonstrates how AI can automate vulnerability validation and patch generation, with human researchers reviewing fixes before submission to maintainers. OpenAI has developed an autonomous AI pipeline that can identify software vulnerabilities, develop working exploits to validate their impact and generate patches for human review. In an October experiment targeting the Linux kernel, the pipeline created exploits for 948 distinct local privilege-escalation (LPE) vulnerabilities at a total API cost of $1.2 million, the company said in a November 4 research report, “A thousand fewer paths to root.”. Human researchers still review the root-cause analysis, proof-of-concept exploits and proposed fixes before findings are reported to maintainers, OpenAI said. Announcing the project in June as part of its Daybreak cybersecurity effort, the company said GPT-5.5 Cyber had identified Linux kernel vulnerabilities and developed 24 LPE exploits. The latest campaign identified five times more unique LPE vulnerabilities than an earlier experiment using GPT-5.6 Sol, despite three months of additional hardening of the Linux kernel between the scans, OpenAI said.

highlights: Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOGL) has nearly caught Anthropic in a demanding new AI benchmark, with its latest Gemini model delivering almost the same performance at roughly one-third the price.
The new benchmark from SemiAnalysis puts Google's Gemini 4 Carbon just behind Anthropic's flagship Claude Opus 5.5, but ahead of OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra.
The result marks a significant advance for Google, which is challenging its biggest AI rivals on both performance and price.
